title: Keepers of the Coast
description: A one-minute look at how lighthouses guided sailors home for centuries.

scenes.narration: For thousands of years, sailors trusted their lives to a single point of light on the horizon.
The great Pharos of Alexandria, built in the third century BC, burned wood fires visible thirty miles out to sea.
By the nineteenth century, spinning Fresnel lenses turned a simple oil lamp into a beam that could pierce fog and storm.
Keepers lived in isolation for months, climbing the tower every few hours to keep the light alive.
Today, satellites and automation have replaced the keepers. But the towers still stand, and their lights still turn.
